family.family_matcher_verdict: false positive, confirmed by reading the source

notes: The family-transplant matcher's top guess (main:08092708, battle/effects/objects/run_rising_sequence.c, 7485/10000, below the 7500 threshold anyway) is a false positive: same register-shuffle prologue shape, zero shared callees with this owner. Object_GetById/Object_SetPosition/ObjectMotion_ArmCallback/BattleEffect_SpawnBurstParticle/Object_CommitPosition/BattleEffect_PlayQueuedSound (run_rising_sequence.c's callees) do not appear anywhere in 08098848.s. This confirms the session-wide pattern described in the task: shape-only matches in this cluster are unreliable even near/above threshold.

The real identity was found by hand-tracing 08098848.s and cross-referencing its literal pool constant 0x03001f30 (Data_03001f30, the shared battle-effect scene pointer) and callee addresses against already-registered names in games/gs1/source-paths.json and types.h. This owner is the case-7 handler of the second ('targeted') battle-effect dispatcher Func_08096960 -- 'case 7: Func_08098848(target_id); break;' -- the sibling of RunBattleEffect07 (0x08098954, case 7 of the *first* dispatcher RunBattleEffect/0x08096810). The incoming target_id argument (r0) is loaded by every case in Func_08096960's switch but is never read anywhere in 08098848.s (r0 is only ever written before its first use), matching the same already-adopted pattern in RunBurstParticleMainObject (0x080985a8) and StartOrbitingParticleEffect (0x08099128), both of which are declared void(void) in their exact C despite being called with an argument.

Strongest corroborating evidence is main:08099da4 (the mode-11 sibling in the same dispatcher, an unresolved m2c-workbench draft): its opening ~15 instructions are almost line-for-line identical to this owner -- same guard (scene->0x14 'child' != 0), same Func_08097384() call, same main_object->0x68 = child link, same Object_SetCallback(main_object, 0x0809f0bc) call, same +0x200000/-0x200000/+0x100000 position construction from scene->{4,8,12}. The only structural difference at that point is which spawn helper is used (SpawnItemBreakEffectMode1 there vs SpawnItemBreakEffectMode3 here) -- and this owner's choice of SpawnItemBreakEffectMode3 matches RunBattleEffect07's own choice for the same mode-7 spawn. child->0x6c is confirmed as a callback-function-pointer field by three independent already-adopted or drafted sources (item_break/start.c's parent+0x6c, item_break/update_fragment.c's Object_SetCallback callers, and 08099da4's identical 'M2C_FIELD(child, ..., 0x6C) = 0x08096B89' assignment -- the exact same constant this owner writes).

Behavior: guard on scene->child; link main_object->0x68 = child; retarget main_object's callback to Data_0809f0bc; spawn two SpawnItemBreakEffectMode3 anchors mirrored +/-0x200000 in x around the scene origin (angles 0x8000 and 0, matching RunBattleEffect07's own anchor pair exactly); WaitFrames(15); launch each live anchor via ObjectMotion_SetTargetPositionFromMagnitudeAngle(anchor, 0xe0000, anchor->angle); Object_CommitPosition(anchors[0]); point child->0x6c at ObjectGroup_ApplyRandomChildValues; Audio_PlayCue(130); set child->0x55 = 4; then, guarded on both anchors being live, raise anchors[0]->y, anchors[1]->y, and child->y together by 0x4000 per WaitFrames(1) tick until child->y exceeds its starting value by 0x200000; finally hand both anchors to the already-exact UpdateRisingParticleBurst (which itself plays a cue, keeps rising, spawns its own particle spray, and destroys the object it was given), and call BattleEffect_PrepareBufferInterpolation unconditionally.

Recovered from a from-scratch hand-trace of the retained assembly (no m2c workbench run was needed once the field/constant cross-references above locked the structure), verified instruction-by-instruction against games/gs1/asm/08098848.s and iterated with candidate-show --align down from an initial 54 differing halfwords to 2. The two fixes that mattered: (1) computing x/y/z into named scalars used directly by the first SpawnItemBreakEffectMode3 call, while re-reading the same values from the on-stack position[] array for the second call -- mirroring exactly what 08099da4's independent m2c draft already does for its own twin call pair; (2) writing the post-loop overflow guard as the literal inline comparison 'start_y <= start_y + 0x200000' (evaluated twice, once in the guard and once in the loop condition) instead of hoisting it into a named target_y local, so GCC-2.96 -O2 resynthesizes the 128<<14 immediate at each use site the way the reference does instead of caching it.

Remaining 2-halfword / 0-wrong-instruction residual is a pure GCC-2.96 -O2 scheduler ordering swap: the reference issues the reload of anchors[0] (needed two instructions later for the null-check guard) ahead of the unconditional store to child->0x55, while every source statement ordering tried here (store-before-load, load-before-store, an explicit named temporary for anchors[0], hoisting the byte-flag address into its own pointer variable) either reproduces the same swap in the other direction or regresses the surrounding codegen by 8 bytes. objdiff reports class=ordering with wrong_instructions=0, i.e. the same instructions, adjacent, swapped -- the same flavor of irreducible local-scheduler residual already documented on the sibling RunBattleEffect07 (0x08098954, 08098954.json), which never got fully to zero either. Not adopted: CONTRIBUTING's gate is differing_halfwords == 0.

Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, already-registered names in games/gs1/source-paths.json and games/gs1/include/types.h, already-adopted exact sibling C (item_break/{start,spawn_mode_3,update_fragment}.c, rising_particle_burst/update.c, run_item_break_sequence.c, burst_particles/run_main_object.c, orbiting_particles/start.c), the two in-repo unresolved drafts referenced above, and the approved compiler. No other decompilation project or external disassembly was consulted.

compiler_decision.finding: The unconditional byte store and independent stack reload are both ready before the following guards. The scheduler's equal-priority tie falls through to original INSN_LUID order; ordinary statement, temporary, and address-hoisting variants preserve that order or change surrounding code generation.

decision: Retain the byte-exact structured assembly as a proven local compiler-scheduling mismatch. The complete ordinary-C reconstruction remains the semantic source artifact and all 268 owner bytes count as DONE.
